    {
      "startEvent": 578,
      "endEvent": 580,
      "contextStartEvent": 507,
      "contextEndEvent": 597,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "this certainly would not be enough for any intelligent person to accept",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Calling acceptance incompatible with intelligence could discredit disagreement independently of its merits. However, A supplies reasons concerning contradictions, myth, and evidential proportionality at E507–577, then another analogy at E585–597. The wording does not clearly make a critic's supposed defect a substitute for evaluating those reasons."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1155,
      "endEvent": 1161,
      "contextStartEvent": 1145,
      "contextEndEvent": 1194,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "so I don't answer hypothetical questions like that",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B explicitly excludes the hypothetical command because he considers it incompatible with God's character, potentially shielding obedience from A's proposed test. Yet E1175–1194 supplies a theological account of goodness and moral knowledge. Rejecting a counterfactual regarded as impossible does not establish immunity to relevant actual evidence; E1157–1159 also contains an apparent transcription error."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1257,
      "endEvent": 1263,
      "contextStartEvent": 1195,
      "contextEndEvent": 1281,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "I prefer to talk about what we actually have evidence for",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After A renews the personal obedience question, B again excludes counterfactual examination and appeals to God's character. This potentially protects the position from a relevant consistency test. However, E1222–1249 offers a bounded Abraham interpretation, and E1277–1280 raises identification of divine speech; neither commits B to dismissing every actual moral counterexample."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1547,
      "endEvent": 1551,
      "contextStartEvent": 1516,
      "contextEndEvent": 1579,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "I think it's difficult to make moral judgments",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B invokes an omniscient being's access to future consequences without identifying consequences that justify the killings. This could shelter the command through unseen reasons, but he says judgment is difficult, not impossible. At E1558–1560 and E1576–1579 he expressly concedes difficulty and A's good point, leaving the objection live."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2101,
      "endEvent": 2108,
      "contextStartEvent": 2075,
      "contextEndEvent": 2108,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "in which case we should throw the book out",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The repeated conclusion rejects the book whether the offending passages are authentic or corrupted. A supplies separate reasons: moral conflict and impaired reliability for induction. What remains unclear is whether 'throw the book out' means rejecting divine authority or all evidential value. A bounded dilemma alone does not establish protection regardless of merits."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 598,
      "endEvent": 637,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the resurrection does not automatically prove divinity",
      "explanation": "A supports this compact conclusion with explicit hypotheticals separating resurrection from moral authority and truthfulness at E608–627. He provisionally grants resurrection for the argument; the statement identifies an additional inference requiring support."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2020,
      "endEvent": 2058,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "faith is a response to beliefs that you've already concluded or true",
      "explanation": "B explains his definition through interpersonal trust and readings of John and Hebrews. Those interpretations remain disputable, but the concise formulation summarizes supplied reasons rather than replacing them or expressly insulating faith from criticism."
